summary.title: Great Works in Programming Languages
summary.one_liner: A crowd-sourced reading list of influential programming language papers, grouped by how many respondents named them, from Hoare's 1969 axiomatic basis to Wright and Felleisen's 1994 type soundness paper.
takeaways: The page lists papers that Benjamin Pierce's Types list respondents (2004) named as the most important in programming languages, grouped by how many people cited them.

The most-cited works include Hoare's axiomatic basis (1969), Landin's 'next 700 programming languages' (1966), Milner's type polymorphism theory (1978), Plotkin's call-by-name/call-by-value paper (1975), and Reynolds' type structure paper (1974).

Other frequently cited topics include Damas-Milner principal type schemes, Moggi's computational lambda-calculus and monads, Necula's proof-carrying code, and Dijkstra's 'Go to statement considered harmful'.
Entries are given with full bibliographic details, and some have BibTeX links; the list is a starting point for reading in the field.
summary.summary: This page, hosted by Benjamin Pierce at UPenn, collects responses to a September 2004 query asking people to name the five most important papers in programming language research. Contributors are thanked by name, and the list is split into three tiers: works mentioned by many respondents, works mentioned by several, and works mentioned at least once. Each entry gives authors, title, venue, and year, with BibTeX links. The page itself contains no commentary on the papers beyond the bibliographic details.
